explanation: Threatanalysis_output.xml holds the computed output of scanning-lin.py's 18-factor composite risk scoring -- not a raw attack flag, a derived score combining multiple signals (e.g. CPU load + memory pressure, or ransomware detection + honeypot trigger together). Each factor_N entry has a factorname matching rv_ioc_lin.xml's vector_group names and a status score: 0.01 is the baseline/clean floor used throughout this file's template, and any higher value means the underlying combination of conditions was at least partially met -- the score is a sum across that factor's contributing vectors, so it also carries rough magnitude information, not just a yes/no.

metadata.reader: not currently read by the chatbot backend -- only raw Alert.xml is
metadata.caveat: scanning-lin.py compares some of these values as strings not numbers (e.g. Disk_value >= str(float(...) * threshold)), which can misfire depending on value formatting

value_meanings.0.01: Baseline/clean floor -- none of this factor's contributing vectors fired. This is the template default, not a computed zero.
value_meanings.any value above 0.01: This factor's underlying condition combination was at least partially met -- the exact scoring arithmetic (whether it's a sum, an average, or something else) wasn't independently verified, so treat any above-baseline value as 'worth investigating' rather than trying to infer a precise vector count from the number itself.

raw_content_examples.note: Both factors at baseline -- nothing firing.

raw_content_examples.note: factor_2's elevated score means at least one (possibly both) of its contributing signals (Ransom and Honeypot) are active -- the exact per-vector scoring arithmetic scanning-lin.py uses wasn't independently verified in the investigation, only that it produces a composite score rather than a single tag's flat 0/1. Don't assume the specific value maps to a precise vector count without confirming against the actual script logic.
